habitat: Singly or in pairs near water, in suburban gardens, cities and at sewage works. It walks on the ground and wags its tail. If disturbed it perches briefly on a tree, wall, fence or building.
summary: A common resident. Greyish, with a white throat and upper breast and a black breast-band. Shorter-tailed than Mountain Wagtail and greyer than the other wagtails. Northern races have the breast-band absent or vestigial. The call is a loud, cheerful tseep-eep or tseeep. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, so status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Kruger is in the north, where Newman says the breast-band may be absent or vestigial. Grey Wagtail is a comparison Newman names and is not in this list. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Mountain Wagtail has a very long tail, is much paler, and is mostly grey and white with a narrow black breast-band.
African Pied Wagtail is black and white. Cape Wagtail is greyish.
